newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PacDun U.S. unit in new class action.
newsitem.headline: PacDun U.S. unit in new class action.

text.p: Pacific Dunlop Ltd said on Thursday its U.S. unit Accufix Research Institute (ARI) reported that a lawsuit seeking class action on behalf of some U.S. implantees of its pacemaker had been filed against the group.

Accufic said in a statement released by Pacific Dunlop that the class action was on behalf of all U.S. impantees of its Encor 330-854 and Encor 033-856 bioplar passive fixation atrial "J" pacemaker leads.
The Encor leads were withdrawn from the market in late 1995 following five reported incidents of protrusion of a J-shaped retention wire within the lead, Pacific Dunlop said.
The filing sought certification of a class action lawsuit, but no class had been certified, Accufic said.
"We believe this lawsuit is without merit and is an inappropriate subject for a class action," Accufix president Larry Wettlaufer said in a statement.
"The company will vigorously defend against the allegations in the lawsuit," Wettlaufer said.
Pacemaker leads are wires that attach a pacemaker to the heart. The "J" wire in the passive leads is encased within two layers of insulation and two conductor coils, Accufix said.
Accufix said 9,049 of the Encor 330-854 bipolar passive leads were distributed in the U.S. between 1989 and the voluntary recall in September 1995.

It said no Encor 033-856 bipolar passive leads were distributed in the United States. To date, 19 protrusions of the model 330-954 leads had been reported to ARI six of the 19 were reported as injuries: five as "non-specific chest pain" and one as a cardiac tamponade.
Last year, Accufix sold Telectronics Pacing Systems, the Pacific Dunlop subsidiary which ran the implant business in the United States.
